question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

events.description:

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s firm grip on the Chinese Communist Party, military, and elite personnel decisions underpins the near-certain trader consensus that he will remain in office through 2027. At age 73, he has shown no intention of stepping down ahead of the 21st Party Congress expected in late 2027, where analysts across multiple reports anticipate he will secure a fourth term as general secretary. Extensive anti-corruption purges have removed potential rivals from the Politburo, Central Military Commission, and other bodies, while age-based retirement norms are projected to apply mainly to subordinates. No designated successor has emerged, and recent leadership reshuffles emphasize loyalty to Xi’s agenda. The only plausible shifts before 2027 would require an abrupt health crisis or an unprecedented internal challenge capable of upending the current power structure.
